key_insight: Continual learning for deepfake detection can worsen demographic unfairness over time, so preserving accuracy alone is not enough.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical AI systems, model update strategies must be evaluated for both performance stability and fairness across shifting data distributions.
method: Tracked fairness across four dimensions and multiple demographics
Evaluated detectors on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world deepfake generation methods
Compared continual learning families: rehearsal, prompts, and regularization
evidence_signal: The study analyzes fairness metrics over time on progressively trained deepfake detectors using a chronological dataset of 11 generation methods.
watch_item: Fairness gains were rare and inequitable forgetting was not explained by underrepresentation alone, so deployment needs careful demographic monitoring beyond standard accuracy checks.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
